nodes.name: Clinical Presentation
nodes.title: B-Cell Lymphomas: Clinical Presentation & Diagnostic Suspicion
nodes.description: Patients presenting with persistent painless lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, extranodal mass lesions, or systemic B-symptoms.
bullets: Clinical presentation: painless, rubbery peripheral lymphadenopathy (cervical, axillary, inguinal), mediastinal or retroperitoneal mass, splenomegaly, or extranodal involvement (GI tract, skin, thyroid, bone).
B-Symptoms: Unexplained fever >38°C, drenching night sweats, or unexplained weight loss >10% of body weight over 6 months.

options.label: Suspicion of lymphoma - Proceed to mandatory diagnostic workup

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: B-Cell Lymphomas: Biopsy, Pathology, Imaging, and Pre-Treatment Checklist
nodes.description: Excisional lymph node biopsy, comprehensive IHC/FISH panel, whole-body FDG-PET/CT staging, and HBV screening.
bullets: Excisional or Incisional Biopsy (Preferred): Complete lymph node excision is strongly recommended to evaluate tissue architecture; core needle biopsy is acceptable ONLY when lymph nodes are inaccessible for surgical excision. Fine needle aspiration (FNA) alone is INADEQUATE for initial diagnosis.

Comprehensive Immunohistochemistry (IHC) Panel: CD20, CD3, CD5, CD10, BCL2, BCL6, Cyclin D1, SOX11, Ki-67, MYC, IRF4/MUM1. Flow cytometric immunophenotyping to demonstrate light chain restriction (kappa/lambda).
Molecular Cytogenetics & FISH: FISH for IGH::BCL2 t(14;18) (follicular), CCND1::IGH t(11;14) (mantle cell), MYC rearrangement (Burkitt / double-hit), and BCL6 rearrangement.

Staging Imaging: Whole-body FDG-PET/CT (skull base to mid-thigh) is the gold standard for staging FDG-avid lymphomas (Lugano classification) and selecting post-treatment response (Deauville 5-point scale). Diagnostic CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast.
Laboratory Workup: CBC with differential, CMP (renal function, electrolytes, LFTs, uric acid), baseline serum LDH (critical prognostic biomarker), and beta-2 microglobulin.

Mandatory Hepatitis B Screening: HBsAg and anti-HBc total antibody testing mandatory prior to any anti-CD20 therapy (Rituximab, Obinutuzumab); prophylactic antiviral therapy (Entecavir) mandatory if positive to prevent fatal hepatic reactivation.
Infectious disease screening: Hepatitis C antibody, HIV-1/2 serology.
Cardiac Assessment: Transthoracic echocardiogram or MUGA scan to document baseline LVEF prior to anthracycline (doxorubicin) chemotherapy.
Pregnancy test and fertility counseling in patients of reproductive age prior to cytotoxic therapy.

nodes.name: Histologic Subtype
nodes.title: B-Cell Lymphomas: Major Histopathologic Subtypes
nodes.description: Select confirmed diagnosis per 2022 WHO / ICC lymphoma classification.
bullets: Follicular Lymphoma (FL): Indolent germinal center B-cell lymphoma; grades 1, 2, 3A termed classic FL (cFL).
Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL): Cyclin D1+ / t(11;14)+ / SOX11+; aggressive clinical course.
Marginal Zone Lymphoma (MZL): Extranodal MALT, Nodal MZL, or Splenic MZL.
Burkitt Lymphoma (BL): Highly aggressive, starry sky morphology, MYC translocation, Ki-67 ~100%.
Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) / High-Grade B-Cell (HGBL): Most common aggressive lymphoma.

options.label: Marginal Zone Lymphoma (MZL: MALT / Nodal / Splenic)

nodes.name: FL Stage & Burden
nodes.title: Follicular Lymphoma: Stage & GELF Tumor Burden
nodes.description: Distinguish early localized disease from advanced stage or high tumor burden (GELF criteria).
bullets: Early Stage (Stage I or contiguous Stage II): Confined to a single radiation port without systemic symptoms.

Advanced Stage (Stage III–IV or non-contiguous Stage II): Evaluate GELF tumor burden criteria (bulky mass >=7 cm, >=3 nodal sites each >=3 cm, symptomatic splenomegaly, organ compression, pleural effusion/ascites, cytopenias).

options.label: Stage I or Contiguous Stage II (Non-bulky, Localized)
Advanced Stage (Stage III–IV), Low Tumor Burden (GELF Negative)
Advanced Stage (Stage III–IV), High Tumor Burden (GELF Positive / Symptomatic)

nodes.name: Early FL Treatment
nodes.title: Stage I–II Follicular Lymphoma: Definitive Radiation or Observation
nodes.description: Curative-intent local radiation therapy or active surveillance for localized disease.
bullets: Involved-Site Radiation Therapy (ISRT, Preferred): 24–30 Gy to involved nodal region; delivers >90% local control and long-term disease-free survival in localized Stage I FL.
Observation / Active Surveillance: Acceptable in asymptomatic patients when ISRT would entail significant morbidity.
Systemic Immunochemotherapy +/- ISRT: Option for bulky Stage II disease (e.g. Bendamustine + Rituximab).
Surveillance: Clinical exam and labs every 3–6 months for 5 years, then annually.

nodes.name: Low-Burden FL Watch & Wait
nodes.title: Advanced Low-Burden FL: Active Surveillance (Watch and Wait)
nodes.description: Evidence-based deferred therapy for asymptomatic patients without GELF criteria.
bullets: Watchful Waiting / Active Surveillance (Preferred): Deferring treatment until GELF criteria or symptoms develop does NOT compromise overall survival and avoids chemotherapy toxicity.
Single-Agent Rituximab (Optional): Rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly x 4 doses; can be considered for patients with disease-related anxiety or wishing to avoid chemo.
Follow-up: Physical examination, CBC, CMP, and LDH every 3–6 months; cross-sectional imaging only if clinical symptoms or exam suggests progression.

nodes.name: High-Burden FL Frontline
nodes.title: Advanced High-Burden FL: Frontline Chemoimmunotherapy & Maintenance
nodes.description: Frontline regimens for symptomatic, bulky, or GELF-positive follicular lymphoma.
bullets: Preferred First-Line Regimens:
• Bendamustine + Rituximab (BR): Bendamustine 90 mg/m2 IV days 1 & 2 + Rituximab 375 mg/m2 day 1 q28d x 6 cycles. Superior PFS and less alopecia/neuropathy than R-CHOP (StiL trial).
• Bendamustine + Obinutuzumab (G-Bendamustine): Demonstrated superior PFS in GALLIUM trial; requires close infection prophylaxis.
• Lenalidomide + Rituximab (R2): Chemo-free oral doublet; Lenalidomide 20 mg PO days 1-21 + Rituximab weekly x 4 in cycle 1 then q4w (RELEVANCE trial).
• R-CHOP (rchop): Rituximab + Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Vincristine, Prednisone x 6 cycles (favored if suspicion of histologic transformation to large cell).
Maintenance Therapy: In patients responding to induction, Rituximab maintenance (375 mg/m2 every 8-12 weeks for 2 years) prolongs progression-free survival (PRIMA trial).
Infection Prophylaxis: VZV prophylaxis (acyclovir) and PJP prophylaxis (Bactrim) mandatory during and for 6 months after bendamustine.

nodes.name: MCL TP53 Mutation Status
nodes.title: Mantle Cell Lymphoma: TP53 Mutation & Fitness Stratification
nodes.description: Mandatory testing for TP53 mutation or deletion, which predicts chemoresistance and guides targeted frontline therapy.
bullets: TP53 Mutated (or 17p deleted): Chemoresistant biology with poor outcomes after standard cytarabine/ASCT regimens; chemotherapy-free BTK inhibitor combinations preferred.
TP53 Wild-Type: Standard intensive cytarabine/ASCT or non-intensive chemoimmunotherapy based on patient age and performance status.

options.label: TP53 Wild-Type: Fit for Intensive Therapy (Age <65, Good Performance)
TP53 Wild-Type: Unfit / Older Adults (Age >=65 or Comorbidities)

nodes.name: TP53-Mutated MCL Frontline
nodes.title: TP53-Mutated MCL: Targeted Chemotherapy-Free Regimens
nodes.description: Non-chemotherapy BTK inhibitor combinations for TP53-aberrant mantle cell lymphoma.
bullets: Chemo-free Triplet (BOVen / Preferred): Zanubrutinib (or Acalabrutinib) + Venetoclax + Obinutuzumab (or Rituximab); produces high rates of undetectable MRD in frontline TP53-mutated MCL.
BTK Inhibitor + Venetoclax: Ibrutinib or Zanubrutinib combined with Venetoclax.
Avoid standard cytotoxic ASCT: Conventional high-dose chemotherapy + autologous HCT fails to achieve durable remission in TP53-mutated MCL.
Allogeneic HCT Consideration: Consider allogeneic stem cell transplantation in eligible patients achieving remission with targeted therapy.
Enrollment in clinical trials strongly encouraged.

nodes.name: MCL Fit Intensive Frontline
nodes.title: Fit TP53-WT MCL: Cytarabine Induction, ASCT Consolidation & Rituximab Maintenance
nodes.description: Standard intensive curative-intent strategy for young, fit mantle cell lymphoma patients.
bullets: High-Dose Cytarabine-Containing Induction (Preferred):
• Alternating R-CHOP / R-DHAP (LyMa trial / European MCL Network): 3 cycles R-CHOP alternating with 3 cycles R-DHAP (high-dose cytarabine).
• Nordic MCL2 Regimen: Dose-intensified R-CHOP alternating with high-dose cytarabine.
• Hyper-CVAD + Rituximab: Alternating with high-dose methotrexate and cytarabine.
Consolidative Autologous Stem Cell Transplant (ASCT): High-dose BEAM (dlbcl-beam) conditioning with autologous rescue in first complete remission (CR1).
Post-ASCT Maintenance: Rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV every 8 weeks for 3 years (significantly prolongs event-free and overall survival per LyMa trial).
Addition of BTK inhibitor: Incorporation of Zanubrutinib/Acalabrutinib into induction/maintenance per emerging TRIANGLE trial data.

nodes.name: MCL Unfit Frontline
nodes.title: Unfit / Older TP53-WT MCL: Less Intensive Chemoimmunotherapy & BTKi
nodes.description: Dose-tolerable chemoimmunotherapy followed by maintenance for older adults.
bullets: Preferred First-Line Regimens:
• Bendamustine + Rituximab (BR): Bendamustine 90 mg/m2 days 1 & 2 + Rituximab 375 mg/m2 day 1 q28d x 6 cycles.
• VR-CAP: Bortezomib, Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Prednisone (substituting vincristine with bortezomib; LyMa/E1411 standard).
• R-mini-CHOP: Attenuated dose for frail patients aged >80 years.
Maintenance Therapy: Rituximab maintenance (375 mg/m2 every 8-12 weeks for 2 years) or until progression.
Second-Line / Relapse: Covalent BTK inhibitors (Zanubrutinib, Acalabrutinib), non-covalent BTKi (Pirtobrutinib), or CAR T-cell therapy (Brexucabtagene autoleucel).

nodes.name: Marginal Zone Therapy
nodes.title: Marginal Zone Lymphoma (MZL): MALT, Splenic, and Nodal Management
nodes.description: Etiology-directed treatment (H. pylori eradication) and systemic immunotherapy for MZL.
bullets: Gastric MALT Lymphoma: Mandatory Helicobacter pylori testing (biopsy, breath test, stool antigen); first-line treatment is antibiotic eradication therapy. Re-endoscopy at 3 months; if persistent MALT and H. pylori-negative, administer ISRT (24–30 Gy).
Nongastric Extranodal MALT: Local ISRT (24 Gy) produces high cure rates; reserve systemic therapy for disseminated disease.
Splenic MZL: Test for Hepatitis C virus (HCV treatment can induce lymphoma remission); for symptomatic splenomegaly/cytopenias, Rituximab monotherapy (375 mg/m2 weekly x 4) or splenectomy.
Systemic / Disseminated MZL: Managed similar to follicular lymphoma: Bendamustine + Rituximab (BR), single-agent Rituximab, or Lenalidomide + Rituximab (R2).

nodes.name: Burkitt Lymphoma Regimens
nodes.title: Burkitt Lymphoma: Intensive Chemoimmunotherapy & CNS Prophylaxis
nodes.description: High-intensity multiagent protocols curative for Burkitt lymphoma.
bullets: Mandatory Emergency TLS Prophylaxis: Aggressive IV hydration, Rasburicase (recombinant urate oxidase), and inpatient telemetry prior to starting therapy.
Preferred First-Line Regimens:

• Dose-Adjusted EPOCH + Rituximab (dlbcl-da-epoch-r): Etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin + rituximab; highly effective with lower treatment-related mortality in both adults and elderly (NCI protocol).
• CODOX-M / IVAC + Rituximab: Cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin, high-dose methotrexate alternating with ifosfamide, etoposide, high-dose cytarabine.
• Hyper-CVAD + Rituximab: Fractionated cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin, dexamethasone alternating with methotrexate and cytarabine.
CNS Prophylaxis (Mandatory): Systemic high-dose methotrexate/cytarabine combined with intrathecal methotrexate or triple IT therapy (methotrexate, cytarabine, corticosteroid).
Avoid standard R-CHOP: R-CHOP is INADEQUATE for Burkitt lymphoma and results in unacceptably high relapse rates.

nodes.name: DLBCL / HGBL Management
nodes.title: Diffuse Large B-Cell & High-Grade B-Cell Lymphomas: Frontline & Novel Regimens
nodes.description: Curative-intent frontline chemoimmunotherapy and targeted bispecifics / CAR-T.
bullets: Preferred First-Line Regimens:
• Pola-R-CHP (dlbcl-pola-r-chp): Polatuzumab vedotin (CD79b ADC) + Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Prednisone x 6 cycles; Category 1 preferred for IPI >=2 (POLARIX trial).
• R-CHOP (rchop): Category 1 standard for IPI 0-1 or low-risk disease.
High-Grade B-Cell Lymphoma with MYC and BCL2/BCL6 (Double-Hit / Triple-Hit):
• Dose-Adjusted EPOCH-R (dlbcl-da-epoch-r) is preferred over R-CHOP.
Relapsed / Refractory Disease (<12 months or refractory):
• CD19 CAR T-Cell Therapy: Axicabtagene ciloleucel or Lisocabtagene maraleucel (Category 1 preferred over salvage chemo/ASCT per ZUMA-7 and TRANSFORM trials).
• CD20xCD3 Bispecific Antibodies: Epcoritamab (dlbcl-epcoritamab) or Glofitamab (dlbcl-glofitamab) for >=2 prior lines.
• Tafasitamab + Lenalidomide (dlbcl-tafa-len) or Loncastuximab tesirine (dlbcl-loncastuximab).
